note: Both sets capture the same core facts correctly: TV display minimum 27 in. (68.6 cm), computer display minimum 15 in. (38.1 cm), TV brightness at least 75% of maximum, simultaneous/independent operation, and the 8-person dinner count with its composition condition. Neither set contains a misread, misbound or invented claim. Set A, however, adds two further restatements of the display-size facts under a second attribute name ('minimum size' 38.1 cm and 68.6 cm) that Set B omits, so A carries more redundancy for no added information. Set B is therefore marginally better as the leaner set with the same correct content.
remarks: Both sets state each display size three times (in., cm, and again under 'minimum size'), a systematic duplication pattern in the extractor. Both also miss several substantive facts on the page: the computer may be a laptop or desktop, there is no required volume setting, the meal must be served/eaten in the finished square footage at the designated eating area, and the whole safety list in 9-3k (no flames, no alcohol, sealed drinking water, hot-water-and-soap washing, proper storage/refrigeration, ingredient lists for allergies, no outdoor cooking equipment use on site, no coolers on site). The brightness condition 'during home electronics tasks' is a reasonable binding to rule 9-4b, though the rule text itself does not state that condition explicitly.
